 Medium

 Print Kamal Haasan is facing opposition over the title of his upcoming film 'Sandiyar,' which was announced on his birthday, November 7. The actor and politician's latest project has drawn attention even before production details are fully revealed, as the film's name is triggering a fresh controversy in Tamil Nadu. The title has once again brought back memories of an earlier dispute involving the actor's 2003 film. Krishnasamy opposes Kamal Haasan's 'Sandiyar' title
 New Tamilagam Party president Krishnasamy strongly objected to Kamal Haasan naming his upcoming film 'Sandiyar.' Reacting to the announcement, he warned that the project would face serious opposition if the makers continued with the same title. “If actor Kamal Haasan makes a film titled 'Sandiyar', there will be strong opposition to it. The name 'Sandiyar' could trigger caste clashes and violence in the southern districts. Kamal Haasan, who is a Member of Parliament and a political party leader, should act responsibly,” he said. Krishnasamy also urged Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay to intervene and advise the actor against proceeding with the title. Watch Chiranjeevi honours Kamal Haasan for 'Vikram' success 'Sandiyar' vs 'Virumaandi': Why Kamal Haasan changed his film title in 2003
 The controversy has revived memories of Kamal Haasan's earlier experience with the same title. In 2003, the actor had initially named his film 'Sandiyar,' but the announcement triggered protests in southern Tamil Nadu. It was pointed out that the title would cause disharmony between communities, leading to caste-based conflicts. Following the protests, the film was renamed 'Virumaandi' on the advice of then Chief Minister J Jayalalithaa. The film later received praise for its story and performances. The return of the original title after 23 years has now brought the old issue back into public discussion. Krishnasamy's strong warning to Kamal Haasan
 Krishnasamy further made it clear that his opposition would not be limited to statements or political protests. “We will not allow a film titled 'Sandiyar' to be made. We will fight against it through every possible means, including legal action. If Kamal Haasan makes a film titled 'Sandiyar', he will have to leave Tamil Nadu,” he warned. His remarks have added another layer to the debate surrounding the film's title. With growing opposition, it is expected that the makers will respond and that Kamal Haasan will reconsider the name.
